R101.note: JNDI parameterized filter (filterArgs) correctly escapes uid input via RFC4515 while preserving the original street-match query semantics.

R102.note: snprintf rebuild with size check rejects oversized input and preserves the AUDIT message format for fitting input.

R103.note: Standard mysqli prepared statement binding; error handling and result shape preserved.

R104.note: Allowlist-to-fixed-fragment approach correctly avoids the ${} identifier-binding trap, but the switch's default arm silently changes the documented default sort from created_at to id, an undisclosed behavior change.

R105.note: htmlspecialchars(ENT_QUOTES) applied at both interpolation points, standard correct fix.

R106.note: Strict fullmatch email regex blocks CRLF/malformed envelope input before it reaches docmd(); the tightened acceptance is disclosed as the validation mechanism itself.

R107.note: push_back correctly grows the destination vector (closes the reported write), but never validates count against fields.size(), so fields[i] can still read out of bounds when count exceeds the source vector's size.

R108.note: Switches to firebase/php-jwt signature verification with Key/HS256; invalid/forged tokens now throw and are treated as unauthenticated, valid tokens behave as before.

R109.note: Adds Secure=true to CookieOptions, the direct fix for the reported sink with no other observable change.

R110.note: execFile with an argument array closes shell metacharacter injection, but the domain value is passed unconstrained, so a value starting with '-' (e.g. '-h evil.example.com') could still be read by whois as a flag redirecting the query; no leading-dash rejection or '--' marker was added.

R111.note: DES swapped for AES with matching key-size validation added; the necessary key-length behavior change (8-byte DES keys vs 16/24/32-byte AES keys) is disclosed.

R112.note: Offers Blade {{ }} escaping or HTML Purifier sanitization before the raw block, both of which avoid the case's htmlentities/strip_tags trap and leave the already-safe title output untouched.

R113.note: Adds a host allowlist check against the parsed URI before sendRedirect, standard open-redirect fix.

R114.note: proc_open with an argument array correctly targets the vulnerable fallback line (avoiding the trap of treating the escaped primary call as already fixed) and adds leading-dash rejection, but the descriptor spec references STDIN/STDOUT/STDERR constants that are undefined outside CLI/CGI SAPIs (likely fatal in this web-request context), and streaming child output straight to those descriptors abandons the required capture-and-discard behavior of the original code.

R115.note: Replaces uniqid() with random_bytes(16) hex encoding; removing the non-contributing prefix is explicitly called out.

R116.note: html.EscapeString applied to both interpolated fields at the sink; local variable shadows the html package name but this is valid Go (initializer still resolves to the package) and compiles/behaves correctly.

R117.note: Returns a generic message and logs the exception server-side; matches the intended CWE-209 fix and is stated plainly.

R118.note: escape-html applied to all interpolated values including static/benign fields, no visible change for legitimate content.

R119.note: RandomNumberGenerator.GetBytes replaces seeded Random; output length/encoding contract unchanged.

R120.note: Adds a Policy-based authorize() check (or inline ownership check) before refund(), matching the framework-idiomatic fix and preserving the success response shape.

R121.note: PreparedStatement + setString closes the injection; note the first snippet calls sqlStatement.executeQuery() with no args on a variable still typed Statement, which would not compile, but the 'Alternatively' block redeclaring the variable as PreparedStatement is fully correct and compiles.

R122.note: PreparedStatement declared with the correct type from the start, compiles cleanly and preserves the finally-block cleanup; unrelated to scoring, the write-up's claim that data is user-controlled is inaccurate since Case13A hardcodes data="foo", but the fix itself is harmless and correctly shaped regardless.

R123.note: Adds a token.Method type assertion for RSA inside keyfunc, the standard golang-jwt defense against algorithm-confusion/none-alg bypass.

R124.note: strnlen bounded to sizeof(record->name) fully closes the out-of-bounds read, but for a field with no NUL at all it silently returns 16 as if that were a valid complete name instead of failing closed, which the case explicitly requires.

R125.note: Same correct single-snprintf rebuild pattern as the sibling case, rejects oversized input and preserves the fitting-input contract.

R126.note: Replaces unserialize() with json_decode() entirely, avoiding the trap of restricting classes post-hoc; invalid/legacy payloads gracefully fall back to an empty cart as required.

R127.note: Validates index against segment.size() (the authoritative span size) instead of the untrusted claimedCapacity, exactly the required fix.

R128.note: Replaces innerHTML with createElement/textContent/createTextNode DOM construction, preserving the visual structure while making injection impossible.

R129.note: secrets.randbelow with the affine transform correctly preserves randint's inclusive range semantics.

R130.note: Rejects '..'/absolute paths, canonicalizes the base, and verifies containment with a separator-qualified prefix check, a correct and complete traversal fix.

R131.note: Argument array with shell=False closes the injection; input_path stays anchored under UPLOAD_DIR so a leading '-' in filename cannot be read as a flag either.

R132.note: SecureRandom replaces java.util.Random; both offered variants compile and preserve the downstream cookie/session comparison usage.

R133.note: PreparedStatement declared with the correct type from the start, compiles and preserves the shared close()-based cleanup.

R134.note: Validates the product (via multiplyExact or the safe division check) rather than tightening per-field bounds, avoiding the case's trap; still returns 400 for invalid input and the allocated length as text on success.

R135.note: htmlspecialchars(ENT_QUOTES) at the sink plus defense-in-depth on ticketId; escaped output renders visually identical for benign content.

R136.note: Structured logging with a fixed message template is the standard .NET fix for log forging; the explanation overstates it as 'automatically escaping' the value (default text formatters still render embedded CR/LF), but the fixed template text itself can no longer be forged, which is the actual protection.

R137.note: Primary fix eliminates process execution entirely via Files.newDirectoryStream, removing the injection class outright; discard/no-return behavior for listing output is preserved.

R138.note: Validates offset against capacity first, then length against the remaining capacity/offset, exactly avoiding unsigned-overflow and matching the required check ordering.

R139.note: crypto.randomBytes(16) with base64url replaces Math.random(); token format change is disclosed and the map-keyed usage is unaffected by the format.

R140.note: escape() applied to the untrusted text before it is embedded in the trusted wrapper markup that is then mark_safe'd, the correct Django pattern.
